description: How a phone applies what comes back from the server (Android and iOS). Given its local state (feed position `after`, entities with their known server versions, the queue, open conflicts) and one step (a changes page, the receipts for the queue's sent commands, or the user resolving a conflict), the local state afterwards and any notices for the user. Page: each change to an entity with a queued command or an open conflict updates only its known version (and the conflict's server copy); otherwise an active change is stored (unless older than the known version) and a delete removes the entity or is ignored if unknown; then after = next_after. The page is applied in one transaction. Receipts, matched in order to the sent commands, each remove its command: applied records the version and closes any conflict; duplicate acts as its original; conflict keeps the local document, drops later unsent commands for the entity and opens a conflict; merged moves every local use of the tag ID to the surviving tag; gone removes the entity; rejected restores the server's copy (or removes the entity when there is none) and adds a notice. Removing a custom dhikr removes its dhikr_personal; removing a tag removes it from local dhikr_personal documents and unsent commands. Resolve keep_mine queues the local version (or delete) on the server's version; use_theirs takes the server's copy.

entities.description: Entities present on the phone (deleted ones are gone), sorted by entity_type, then entity_id. known_version is the last server version seen; 0 if the server hasn't confirmed it yet.

conflicts.description: Open conflicts, sorted by entity_type, then entity_id. local_op is put if the entity exists locally, else delete.

command_id.description: The new command's ID for keep_mine; null for use_theirs.

cases.description: Changes without local edits are applied as they come: an update replaces the document and known version, a new entity is added, and after moves to next_after.

cases.description: A delete removes the entity; the server sends the cascaded dhikr_personal delete as its own change.
A delete of something this phone never had is ignored.
A new profile reads from after=0 and stores everything it gets.
A change to an entity with a queued local edit updates only its known version. The local document and the queued command (still on version 3) stay; the conflict surfaces when it's sent.
A change to an entity deleted locally but not yet sent doesn't bring it back.
The phone's own applied change comes back in the feed with the server's document, which wins: here the server rewrote a merged tag ID.
A change older than the version this phone already knows is ignored.
A change to an entity with an open conflict refreshes the conflict's server copy and the known version; the local document stays.

cases.description: applied: the command leaves the queue and the entity's known version becomes the receipt's.
A later unsent command for the same entity stays queued; it was already chained on the version this receipt confirms.
duplicate is handled as its original receipt (here a resend after a lost response).
conflict: the local edit stays, an open conflict records the server's copy for Keep mine / Use theirs, and later unsent commands for the entity are dropped (the local document already holds them).

cases.description: A local delete that conflicts records local_op delete; the entity stays deleted locally until the user chooses.
merged into a tag this phone hasn't pulled yet: the local tag takes the surviving ID, name and version, and every local use of the old ID (dhikr_personal documents and unsent commands) is rewritten.
merged into a tag this phone already has: the duplicate local tag goes, its uses are rewritten without repeats, and unsent commands for the merged tag are dropped.
gone: the entity was deleted elsewhere. It's removed locally with its unsent commands, and a custom dhikr's dhikr_personal goes with it.
rejected: the entity goes back to the server's copy and the user is told (a notice with the code).
A rejected create has no server copy, so the entity is removed; a removed tag is also taken out of local dhikr_personal documents and unsent commands.
Receipts match the sent commands one to one, in order; unsent commands wait for the next batch.
Keep mine: the local document is queued again on the server's version.

cases.description: Use theirs: the server's copy replaces the local edit and nothing is queued.
